Topics

What we'll cover

Sessions follow your exam board's specification and your target grade. These are the main areas.

Theme 1: Markets and market failure

  • How markets work: supply, demand and elasticity
  • Market failure
  • Government intervention

Theme 2: The UK economy

  • Measures of economic performance
  • Aggregate demand and aggregate supply
  • Economic growth
  • Macroeconomic objectives and policies

Theme 3: Business behaviour and the labour market

  • Business growth and objectives
  • Revenues, costs and profits
  • Market structures
  • The labour market

Theme 4: A global perspective

  • International economics
  • Poverty and inequality
  • Emerging and developing economies
  • The financial sector and the role of the state

Themes shown are for Edexcel A, the specification I sat. AQA and OCR group the same ideas differently, so we follow your board's structure.

The exams

How the exams work

Edexcel A has three papers. Paper 1 is Markets and business behaviour (Themes 1 and 3), Paper 2 is The national and global economy (Themes 2 and 4), and Paper 3 is Microeconomics and macroeconomics: the synoptic paper, drawing on all four themes.

Across all of them, marks go to diagrams that are explained, chains of reasoning, quantitative skills and evaluation.

Exam technique

Where marks are usually lost

  • Describing a point without developing it into a chain of reasoning
  • Evaluation that could apply to any case, rather than the context given
  • Diagrams that are drawn but not explained
  • Data-response answers that don't use the extract

FAQ

A-level Economics: common questions

I'm on AQA or OCR, not Edexcel. Can you still help?

Yes. Sessions are tailored to whichever board your school sits. Edexcel A is the specification I sat myself.

What is Paper 3?

On Edexcel A, Paper 3 is the synoptic paper, bringing together micro and macro across all four themes. I scored 96% in it.

Do I need to be good at maths for Economics?

Some quantitative skills are examined (elasticity, the multiplier, real versus nominal figures), but they're a small part of the course. We cover them as they come up.
